The sem engine: constraints and the MBCO test

Source: vignettes/articles/model-sem-constraints.qmd

Fix, bound or equate parameters, and test the indirect effect with one call. Part of the Models collection; the third of five sem engine pages.

What it does equality, inequality and fixed-value constraints on labeled paths, linear or nonlinear; mbco_sem() for the indirect effect; anova() for nested fits
Class returned SEMFit
Syntax a == b, a + b == 1, a < 0.3, y ~ 0.5 * x, CONSTRAINT(a == b)
Limit a sum of products such as a1 * b1 + a2 * b2 == 0 is best-effort (see Limits) 
base <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2
"

Equal paths

Write the constraint on its own line, bare or inside CONSTRAINT():

free <- fit_sem(paste0(base, "ab := a * b"), mediation_demo)
equal <- fit_sem(paste0(base, "CONSTRAINT(a == b)\nab := a * b"), mediation_demo)
rbind(free = coef(free)[c("a", "b")], constrained = coef(equal)[c("a", "b")])
                    a         b
free        0.5826425 0.5711384
constrained 0.5737394 0.5737394

The constrained fit has one more degree of freedom, and summary(equal) lists the constraint as active under Diagnostics.

Bounds and fixed values 

bounded <- fit_sem(paste0(base, "a < 0.3\nab := a * b"), mediation_demo)
round(coef(bounded)[c("a", "b")], 4)
     a      b
0.3000 0.5711 
fixed <- fit_sem(sub("cp \\*", "0 *", paste0(base, "ab := a * b")), mediation_demo)
round(coef(fixed)[c("a", "b")], 4)
     a      b
0.5826 0.5996

a < 0.3 pushed a onto the bound, and cp was fixed at 0 in the second fit. A parameter that sits on a bound has a standard error of 0 in the table; read the “Active bounds” line of summary() before using it.

Test the indirect effect

mbco_sem() is the minimum-of-two likelihood-ratio test (MBCO): it refits with a fixed at 0 and with b fixed at 0, and the smaller statistic tests \(a \, b = 0\).

mbco_sem(free, "a", "b")

    Minimum-of-two likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect

data:  a * b = 0
MBCO = 33.63, df = 1, p-value = 6.666e-09

The result is an htest; the two component tests are in its tests element. For a chain, name every path: mbco_sem(fit, paths = c("a", "d", "b")) is the minimum of the single-path tests for \(a \, d \, b = 0\), referred to a chi-square with 1 degree of freedom.

A refit that cannot be fitted does not stop mbco_sem(). This happens, for example, when the null a = 0 contradicts a constraint already in the model (a > 0.3). The failed refit is a row of tests with converged = FALSE and the reason in note, a warning repeats it, and the statistic and p-value are NA rather than the smaller of the refits that worked. Check res$unresolved before reading the p-value; the troubleshooting guide shows the result.

Nonlinear constraints

A constraint may be nonlinear in the labels. Setting cp equal to the indirect effect is one:

tied <- fit_sem(paste0(base, "CONSTRAINT(cp == a * b)\nab := a * b"), mediation_demo)
round(coef(tied)[c("a", "b", "cp")], 4)
     a      b     cp
0.5443 0.5481 0.2984

Nonzero-product equality

A single equality such as a*b == 0.1 now searches both sign branches independently, using the existing optimizer and acceptance gates. The factors must be distinct free labels, possibly reached through definitions, with no other constraint involving either factor. A finite nonzero constant multiplier is supported too. Bounds may rule out a branch; if a required branch remains unresolved, the call stops rather than returning the best survivor. More than one product equality, a repeated factor or a coupled constraint retains local search.

The internal fit@internals$search_evidence records branch coverage separately from the outcome ledger. charted means the required sign domains were covered, not that a global optimum was proved. Existing optimum statuses retain their meanings, while actual start counts can increase because each nonempty branch gets its own starts. See the algorithm description for coverage limitations and the existing-reference-only residual diagnostic.

Compare nested fits

anova() is the likelihood-ratio test for two nested SEMFits and refits nothing; you vouch that the restriction is nested in substance.

anova(tied, free)
Likelihood-ratio (chi-square difference) test for SEMFit models

n = 400; Chisq is n times the minimized discrepancy

     Df Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
free  0 0.000
tied  1 0.911    0.91097       1     0.3399

Limits

  • Nonlinear constraints are solved with their Jacobian recomputed at every point. cp == a * b and a * b > 0.1 work; a nonlinear inequality can be feasible on several disjoint pieces (a * b > 0.1 holds for two positive or two negative paths), so every start is tried and the best one kept, with a warning when the starts disagree. A sum of products such as a1 * b1 + a2 * b2 == 0 is best-effort (no exact reduction exists): treat the fit as the best of the starts, and raise n_starts when the warning appears.
  • A zero product that cannot be fitted stops the fit. a * b == 0 is solved as one fit per factor; if any branch cannot be fitted, fit_sem() stops with an error (zero-product branches did not converge) instead of returning the best of the others, which need not be the constrained optimum. mbco_sem() reports the same situation in a refit as an unresolved row (see above).
  • A constraint needs a free parameter and labels must be defined in the model.
  • Equal labels are one parameter. Giving two paths the same label equates them without a constraint line.
